To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The gut bacterial communities from sentinel birds placed on commercial farms were altered compared to pre-contact birds, and 2) Members of the Reoviridae (Reovirus and Avastrovirus), Picobirnavirus, and Picornaviruses were present in the gut of sentinel birds placed on farms and not in the gut of pre-contact birds.

the intestinal virome of sentinel birds placed on farms revealed the presence of novel enteric viruses that were not present pre-contact and that the intestinal bacterial communities of the sentinel birds placed on commercial farms were altered compared to the pre-contact communities.

the gut microbiome of sentinel birds placed on commercial poultry farms is altered following contact with commercial birds and is characterized by a decrease in the relative abundance of members of the Lactobacillaceae and an increase in the relative abundance members of the Clostridiaceae and Lachnospiriaceae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the enteric microbiome in the health of poultry, and the impact of poultry on the enteric microbiomes of humans and the environment.

characterizing the complex bacterial and viral communities present in the avian gut, with a particular focus on understanding the effects of microbial communities on poultry performance and animal welfare, and on microbes with human health relevance.
understanding the complex microbiome of the poultry gut, the roles of the microbiome in disease, and the potential for the microbiome to impact the health and welfare of humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this metagenomic analysis provides insight into the colonization and alteration of the poultry gut microbiome and virome by members of the bacterial and viral communities circulating in commercial broilers.

the intestinal virome of the contact birds was altered by the presence of members of the Picorna-, Picobirna- and Reoviridae families, and the bacterial community was altered by the increased presence of Lachnospira/Clostridia and Lactobaccillus.
the intestinal virome and bacterial communities in the poultry enteric environment are highly dynamic, with the potential for significant changes to occur in a very short period of time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intestinal microbiome of poultry raised in the environment is highly complex, and that this complex microbial community influences the intestinal colonization by RNA viruses, and that this colonization may influence the intestinal bacterial community.

the intestinal bacterial and RNA viral communities of sentinel birds placed on selected broiler chicken farms were compared to those of pre-contact birds, and revealed colonization by members from the Picornaviridase, Picobirnaividae, Reovidae, and Astrowiridae families that were not present or present in proportionately lower numbers in the pre-contact birds.
we found that the intestinal bacterial communities in the sentinel birds were similar to those of the contact birds, with some differences in the proportions of specific taxa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiome and virome of broiler chickens is dynamic, with changes that can occur in the absence of any obvious disease or other stressor.
there are many novel enteric viruses and bacteria present in the poultry intestine, and the roles they play in poultry health and disease are not well understood.
the poultry gut is a dynamic environment that is colonized by a complex community of viruses, bacteria, and other microorganisms that can influence animal performance.
